name: Bassa-Nge

summary.text: The Bassa-Nge (Bassa Nupe) speak the Tako dialect of Nupe. Tradition places their origin at Gbara, once the capital of the Nupe Kingdom. They live where the Niger meets the Benue, in Bassa LGA and Lokoja, and their ruler, the Etsu Bassa-Nge, sits at Gboloko. Despite the shared name, their language is not related to that of the Bassa-Komo.

ruler.title: Etsu Bassa-Nge
ruler.note: Seat at Gboloko, in Bassa LGA.

areas.note: The second of Bassa LGA’s three main peoples.
Among the indigenous peoples of Lokoja.

history.text: Seat of the Etsu Bassa-Nge. The Bassa-Nge trace their origin to Gbara, the old Nupe capital.

reviewNotes: The Bassa-Nge page says they are the majority in Lokoja; this conflicts with other accounts of Lokoja and is not used.
